## Issue #1017 CI/CD False Positives, False Negatives, Warnings And Errors

Issue [#1017](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1017) requires
the non-passing default-branch run to be fixed at its root cause, and every
false positive, false negative, warning and error in CI/CD to be found,
classified and corrected — using the current Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript and
Python pipeline templates and the Hive Mind CI/CD guidance as the comparison
baseline, and delivering everything in the single prepared pull request.

The run named by the issue reported `CI/CD Pipeline` as `cancelled` and
`Desktop Release` as `skipped`. The reconstruction shows why: a macOS core
slice spent 133 seconds on unbudgeted setup before starting a step whose
480-second budget would have expired 1.3 seconds *after* the job's own
600-second `timeout-minutes` cap. The runner therefore always won the race, and
GitHub reports a `timeout-minutes` kill as `cancelled` rather than `failed` —
the same class of false negative as issue #977, one level down. The general
rule this issue establishes is that **`timeout-minutes` is a backstop, never
the deadline**.

| ID | Requirement | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1017-1 | Fix the non-passing default-branch run at its root cause rather than by raising the cap that hid it. | Implemented: `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh` terminates the command's process group at its deadline and exits 124 with an `::error`, so an overrun reports `failure` rather than `cancelled`. The macOS lane the incident hit has since been reshaped (issue #1039: eight slices; issue #1059: one platform-test runner) and still runs under a 600s budget inside a 30-minute cap; since issue #1111 macOS CI runs only when `FORMAL_AI_NON_LINUX_CI` is `run`, and the release test matrix's macOS leg reports the skip in a notice. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017.rs` (`budget_wrapper_terminates_the_overrun_and_reports_it_as_an_error`, `budget_wrapper_warns_while_the_command_is_still_alive`, `the_macos_lane_selects_a_non_empty_set_of_tests`). |
| R1017-2 | Make "the step budget expires before the job clock it sits under" a checked invariant across every workflow, not a per-job accident. | Implemented: `MAX_BUDGET_SHARE_PERCENT = 70` in `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017.rs`; `every_step_budget_expires_before_the_job_clock_it_guards` and `every_job_declares_a_timeout_or_delegates_to_one_that_does` sweep every job of every workflow, and issue #1081 extended the rule to the sum of the budgets one job can spend (`rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1081.rs`, `the_budgets_a_job_can_spend_together_fit_inside_its_cap`). |
| R1017-3 | Classify every annotation and every warning- or error-shaped line in the collected logs, fix each defect, and state why each remaining diagnostic is kept. | Implemented: the ledger in `dev/log/issues/1017/pulls/1018/README.md` §4 holds twenty-three fixed-defect rows, D1–D21 (D5 split into D5a/D5b, plus D15b), and nine diagnostic classes kept with a stated reason, sourced from the 25 annotations of `annotations/all-annotations.tsv` and the 20,766 lines of `analysis/soft-warnings.txt`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017_evidence.rs` (`every_collected_diagnostic_is_fixed_or_kept_with_a_reason`), which also holds the ledger's counts to the archived files. |
| R1017-4 | Remove the security false negatives: no `cargo audit` ran on the default branch, and a CodeQL run reported success while 1,023 live source files were extracted with errors. | Implemented: a `cargo-audit` job in `.github/workflows/security.yml` runs on every push, pull request and the weekly `schedule:`, and the CodeQL Rust lane pins the extractor sysroot required by `github/codeql#19982`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017.rs` (`every_ignored_advisory_carries_a_proof_that_ci_rechecks`, `codeql_rust_lane_pins_the_extractor_sysroot`, `codeql_skips_archived_evidence_but_still_analyses_compiled_code`). |
| R1017-5 | Remove the security false positive without creating a permanent blind spot. | Implemented: every `ignore` in `.cargo/audit.toml` carries a machine-checkable proof line that `scripts/check-rust-dependencies.sh` re-derives from `cargo tree --invert` on every run, so no ignore is permanent. The RUSTSEC-2026-0235 entry this issue added expired as designed: once `rkyv@0.7.46` left `Cargo.lock` the script reported the proof stale and the entry was removed (`2b5547750`). Issue #1079 added the opposite-direction `blocked-upstream` form, now carried by RUSTSEC-2025-0057 (`fxhash`, reported as web-capture#155). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017.rs` (`every_ignored_advisory_carries_a_proof_that_ci_rechecks`). |
| R1017-6 | Stop diagnostics that a run's own cancellation manufactures, and test the parsers those diagnostics come from. | Implemented: `.github/workflows/links.yml` guards the broken-link error with `!cancelled()` instead of `always()`, and runs `scripts/check-web-archive.test.mjs` before lychee. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017.rs` (`link_report_parser_is_unit_tested_before_it_is_trusted`). |
| R1017-7 | Put every read-only job in a concurrency group so a superseded push releases its runners, without ever cancelling the default branch. | Implemented: `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017.rs` (`superseded_read_only_work_releases_its_runners`) sweeps every job in every workflow — 72 on 2026-10-08 — and forces each exemption (the `release.yml` pipeline verdict and the learning-cycle writer) to be argued in the test rather than left implicit in the YAML. |
| R1017-8 | Compare the complete file tree against all three pipeline templates and the Hive Mind guidance, adopt the applicable practices, and state each deviation explicitly. | Implemented: `dev/log/issues/1017/pulls/1018/README.md` §5 answers all thirteen Hive Mind checklist items and argues each practice not adopted and the single-architecture image deviation, with `analysis/template-diffs/` and immutable template copies under `references/templates/`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017_evidence.rs` (`template_trees_and_the_best_practice_checklist_are_retained`). |
| R1017-9 | Report the shared and upstream defects with reproductions, workarounds and code-level fix suggestions. | Implemented: seven exact report bodies in `dev/log/issues/1017/pulls/1018/upstream-reports/`, each recording the URL it was filed under: the missing step-execution budget in each of the three templates ([rust#135](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/135), [js#137](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/137), [python#60](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/60)); a repository-scale data point for `github/codeql#19982` ([comment 5309221141](https://github.com/github/codeql/issues/19982#issuecomment-5309221141)) with a follow-up carrying the measured before/after counts ([comment 5309264165](https://github.com/github/codeql/issues/19982#issuecomment-5309264165)); the recovered-but-still-fatal toolset timeout ([electron-builder#10091](https://github.com/electron-userland/electron-builder/issues/10091)); and the quadratic `LinkNetwork::parse` ([meta-language#193](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/193)). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017_evidence.rs` (`every_upstream_report_records_where_it_was_filed`). |
| R1017-10 | Add debug output and a verbose mode where the evidence was insufficient, defaulting to off. | Implemented: three verbose modes, each off by default — the `FORMAL_AI_CI_VERBOSE` heartbeat in `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh`; `FORMAL_AI_TRACE_SLOW_INIT`, which reports each whole-source parse with its byte count and duration; and `FORMAL_AI_TRACE_COMMANDS`, which reports a spawned command's resolved path, budget, elapsed time and whether the deadline fired. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017.rs` (`budget_wrapper_heartbeat_is_available_but_off_by_default`) and `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017_evidence.rs` (`the_slow_init_and_command_traces_are_available_but_off_by_default`). |
| R1017-11 | Apply every fix everywhere the defect occurs, not only where it was observed. | Implemented: each fix is pinned by a repository-wide sweep rather than at the site it was observed — `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017.rs` (`every_step_budget_expires_before_the_job_clock_it_guards`, `every_job_declares_a_timeout_or_delegates_to_one_that_does`, `network_installs_under_a_job_cap_own_a_deadline`, `every_base_branch_merge_uses_one_pinned_commit_per_workflow`). The sweeps found two further instances the incident never touched: a job at 1415s of a 1500s cap and a job with no `timeout-minutes` at all. The agent-sandbox fix was applied in both places it existed: `rust/src/agent.rs` and its source-test mirror (`rust/tests/source/source_tests/agent/tests.rs`, `python3_command_runs_from_allowlisted_resolved_path`). On 2026-10-08 the rule reached an instance the sweeps cannot see, a test step in a job that budgets nothing: the layered CI js tier ran the JavaScript suites as one step taking 378s of its 600s cap, and an edit to a suite never woke that tier. The suites now run in two shards, each under a 360s budget, and a suite edit wakes the tier that runs it (`rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1138_layered_ci.rs`, `the_javascript_suites_run_in_budgeted_shards_that_cover_every_file`; `scripts/detect-code-changes.rs`, `a_javascript_suite_change_reruns_the_tier_that_executes_it`). |

Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017_evidence.rs` (`the_archive_and_delivery_documents_name_the_issue_and_its_pull_request`). |

## Issue #1021 Full-Range Coding And Contribution Artifacts

Issue [#1021](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1021) collects
the prompts Formal AI answered wrongly, the capabilities a contribution needs to
land, and the demand that the whole loop be test-covered in one pull request.
See PR #1027 and `docs/case-studies/issue-1021/`.

The rule the issue states first governs every row below: "solve by
generalization, not specialization -- a per-prompt fix that makes one task pass
is a regression against that instruction, not progress". Rows marked **not
delivered** are reported rather than quietly narrowed, per the issue's own "the
bar is not to be met by lowering it".

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1021-1 | Deliver every sub-issue in a single pull request rather than as a backlog. | Implemented: one branch, one pull request (#1027), one composed body that closes #1021. `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/issue_1021.rs` (`issue_1021_requirements_are_written_down_and_traceable`) holds the ROADMAP entry that names that pull request beside every requirement it carried. |
| R1021-2 | Fix the rule that was wrong, never the prompt that exposed it. | Implemented: every routing change lands in a rule with its vocabulary in `data/seed/`, and each is pinned by held-out paraphrases in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1021_behaviour_range.rs` and, on the JavaScript root, in `rust/tests/web/issue-1021-behaviour-range.test.mjs`. |
| R1021-3 | #868: a bare `ls` is the request, not a fragment. | Implemented: `bare_shell_tokens` reads the terminal-command catalog, so an argument-free command routes to `exec_command` (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1021_behaviour_range.rs::a_bare_command_is_the_request`). JavaScript twin: `rust/tests/web/issue-1021-behaviour-range.test.mjs` (`a bare command is the request`). |
| R1021-4 | #866/#867: `Execute ls command` runs `ls`, not `ls command`. | Implemented: The command-naming noun is declared per language in `data/seed/terminal-commands.lino` and stripped before the passthrough (`a_command_naming_noun_is_not_an_argument`). Pinned in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1021_behaviour_range.rs` and on the agentic planner twin in `rust/tests/web/issue-1021-behaviour-range.test.mjs`. |
| R1021-5 | #865: `List me files here` lists files; `Hello` still greets. | Implemented: `rust/src/agentic_coding/directory_listing.rs` composes a listing request from seeded parts in any word order (`a_prose_listing_request_routes_to_ls_in_any_word_order`). The detector is never told which language it is reading, so adding a `language es` block to `data/seed/shell-intents.lino` routed four held-out Spanish word orders with no Rust change -- finding 11 of the case study. Pinned in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1021_behaviour_range.rs` and, held-out Spanish word orders included, on the agentic planner twin in `rust/tests/web/issue-1021-behaviour-range.test.mjs`. |
| R1021-6 | #863: an example request for copy stdin to stdout in Rust is answered with code. | Implemented: `copy_stdin_to_stdout` is a catalogued task like any other, with a verified template in each of the thirteen catalogued languages, so the reported prompt and held-out paraphrases in five natural languages are answered with code (`a_named_exercise_is_answered_as_a_program`) and the `cp stdin stdout` misrouting is gone with it (`a_named_exercise_is_not_a_file_operation`). A task that consumes input carries the input it was verified against into its run command (`the_stdin_answer_prints_the_input_it_was_verified_against`); one that reads nothing keeps its plain run command (`a_task_that_reads_no_input_keeps_its_plain_run_command`). Pinned in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1021_behaviour_range.rs`; the browser worker learns the same task, its templates and its stdin fixture from `data/seed/hello-world-programs.lino` (`installSeedProgramTasks`, `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_program_requests.js`) and pipes the fixture into the run command it prints, pinned in `rust/tests/web/issue-1021-behaviour-range.test.mjs`. |
| R1021-7 | #862: a Rosetta Code URL is a task to solve, not a `cp` operand. | Implemented: The URL is no longer lowered to `cp`, and the exercise it names is solved: `Execute https://rosettacode.org/wiki/Copy_stdin_to_stdout in Rust` reaches the same catalogued task as the prose that names it, and is answered with the same verified program (`a_named_exercise_is_not_a_file_operation`, `a_named_exercise_is_answered_as_a_program`). Pinned in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1021_behaviour_range.rs` and, for the browser worker and the agentic planner, in `rust/tests/web/issue-1021-behaviour-range.test.mjs`. |
| R1021-8 | #723: a request naming PHP Laravel is answered in Laravel, not in PHP-in-general. | Implemented: The catalog's language axis is an *implementation-target* axis: a row may be a framework of another row (`ProgramLanguage::framework_of`), and a request naming both resolves to the more specific one. Laravel is a target of its own -- its own template, file path, check command and run command (`a_framework_named_coding_request_is_answered_in_that_framework`, `every_framework_target_carries_its_own_execution_surface`) -- while composing a program out of catalogued idioms still reads the base language through `base_language`, because Laravel adds no way of sorting a list that PHP does not have. PHP itself joins the catalog with the verified task templates every other catalogued language carries. Pinned in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1021_behaviour_range.rs` and `rust/tests/source/source_tests/coding/catalog/mod/framework_targets.rs`; the browser worker answers the same targets, pinned in `rust/tests/web/issue-1021-behaviour-range.test.mjs`. |
| R1021-9 | #824: a filesystem move it refuses should be performed. | Implemented: operands are filtered by how a path is written rather than by where it points, so an absolute or `~`-relative move is carried out as the verified `mv` recipe while a `..` traversal is still refused (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1021_behaviour_range.rs::a_move_between_absolute_paths_is_performed`, `a_traversing_move_is_not_performed`; agentic planner twin: `rust/tests/web/issue-1021-behaviour-range.test.mjs`). |
| R1021-10 | #943 (E91): guard against harness-created issues before any GitHub write authority. | Implemented: `gh issue create` is on the never-delegated rung of `rust/src/contribution_write_path.rs` and is refused in both opt-in states (`filing_an_issue_is_refused_in_both_states`). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1021_write_path.rs`. |
| R1021-11 | #944 (E92): rungs on the mutating-action ladder. | Delivered on both axes. The publishing rungs are refused-unless-opted-in and never-delegated (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1021_write_path.rs`). The filesystem rungs `824.L1`-`824.L5` join the issue #916 write-effect ladder with the sandbox-reset semantics the issue asks for by name: each rung declares the state it starts from, its directory is emptied and checked to be empty, the declared state is written and then *read back off disk*, and a start that did not land is a `sandbox` violation rather than a silent premise (`experiments/issue_916_write_effect_ladder/test_ladder.py::SandboxResetTests`). All sixteen rungs are green against the real release binary and the ratchet moved 11/11 -> 16/16. |
| R1021-12 | #946 (E94): versioned recoverable memory. | Implemented: `rust/src/memory_revision.rs` captures the bytes of every tracked file *before* a candidate version is written and restores them exactly when it fails, so a self-compile that does not build leaves the workspace on the last version that did (`a_version_that_does_not_compile_leaves_the_previous_one_in_place`). The baseline that judges a version is pinned by digest, and a candidate that edits it is rolled back before its verdict is consulted (`a_candidate_that_edits_a_baseline_test_is_rolled_back_before_it_is_scored`). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1021_recoverable_memory.rs`. |
| R1021-13 | #947 (E95): bounded autonomy with a stuck-recovery limit. | Implemented: `rust/src/bounded_autonomy.rs` bounds a run on an injected clock: `RecoveryLoop::step` answers `Continue` until the limit -- one hour by default -- is spent, then presents the plan and asks (`a_loop_that_never_resolves_stops_at_the_limit_and_asks`). Per-command permission is the default mode and full trust is a separate opt-in, so delegating the commands is not delegating the choices (`full_trust_does_not_arrive_with_the_full_autonomous_mode`). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1021_bounded_autonomy.rs`. |
| R1021-14 | #924 (E77): one real repository change per release landing as a normal reviewed pull request. | **Not delivered by a `solve` run.** The ledger's self-authored share is non-zero for Agent-CLI-authored leaves, but no qualifying run is a `solve` run. This is an event after the merge, not an artifact a commit can carry: it needs a release cycle in which the self-authored workflow (#1091) runs `solve` and its pull request is reviewed and merged, so no change on this branch can produce it. |
| R1021-15 | Produce the changelog fragment a code change needs. | Implemented: `formal_ai::contribution_artifacts::compose` renders it from `data/seed/contribution-artifacts.lino` into the shape `scripts/check-changelog-fragment.rs` accepts. The predicates are data: `data/seed/shell-intents.lino` gives `mv` and `cp` an `effect` block, which is why `cp` is carried out the same way without `cp` appearing anywhere in `rust/src/`, and why the held-out ladder rung `824.L5` passes. A deep destination works because the recipe prepares the destination's parent (`824.L4`); an occupied destination stops the recipe before the action and is reported as the check that stopped it and the status it exited with, rather than as the completion `mv`'s own exit code would have suggested (`824.L2`, `a_move_onto_an_occupied_destination_stops_before_it_acts`). Six crates needed more than a version number, and the code moved rather than the requirement: `sha2` 0.11 returns a digest type without `LowerHex`, so the nine places that rendered a digest by hand now go through `source_fetch::hex_lower` (finding 28). The crate is on edition 2024, which `build.rs` exports so the `rustc` that judges a self-authored version compiles the same language (`the_crate_is_on_edition_2024_and_the_judge_compiles_the_same_edition`). Stable-only was a rule with no gate behind it and now has one: `nothing_in_the_tree_reaches_for_a_nightly_toolchain` refuses a toolchain file, a toolchain action asking for anything but stable, a per-invocation override, a bootstrap variable, and an unstable feature attribute, across every tracked source, script and workflow. Two crates stay where they are on purpose and say why: `command-stream` at the `=0.16.0` issue #1014 pinned, and `@openai/codex` at 0.147.0 while openai/codex#39487 is open. Five lockfile duplicates are inherited from crates that have not published against the newer major, named one by one in finding 29. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1021.rs`. |
| R1021-34 | A gate that reports a failure names the thing that failed, not the healthy things beside it. | Implemented: The `Broken Link Checker` failed three times over links that answer 200, because `extractBrokenUrls` in `scripts/check-web-archive.mjs` located the failing part of lychee's report by searching for one hard-coded `## Errors per input` heading. lychee writes only the sections a run has links for, so a report whose sole failure was a timeout matched nothing and fell back to parsing the whole document, harvesting every healthy redirect in it. Sections are now sliced out by heading and a section counts as failing unless its category is one of the outcomes known to be healthy -- selection by exclusion, so an unrecognised future category is reported rather than silently dropped, because a false positive is loud and a dropped failure is not. The four tests added to `scripts/check-web-archive.test.mjs` cover the shapes the old lookup got wrong (`reports a timeout when the report has no errors section`, `collects failures from every failing section, not just the first`, `treats an unrecognised section as failing`, `ignores the summary table and the healthy sections around it`) and all four fail against the previous parser; `.github/workflows/links.yml` already ran them ahead of lychee, and missed the defect only because every earlier test described a report that has an errors section. The real report from run 32454084765 is kept as a fixture and replayed by `experiments/issue-1021-link-checker-false-positive/reproduce.mjs`. What stays a finding rather than a change: the job still fails whenever lychee exits non-zero, so a lone runner-side timeout reds the gate over a healthy link, and making that non-fatal would be moving a limit. See finding 32. `rust/tests/web/issue-1021-link-checker.test.mjs` replays the committed report of run 32454084765 through `extractBrokenUrls` and holds it to the one link that timed out. |

An Anthropic-compatible surface answers it too, so `rust/src/server.rs` serves both spellings and `matrix_assert_proxy_ok` is left alone -- the same fix issue #671 made for the bare base path, for the same reason. `rust/tests/integration/issue_1021_client_preflight.rs` pins all three probes and was falsified against the unpatched server. See finding 33. |
| R1021-36 | A step that is terminated for running too long reports what made it slow. | Implemented: `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh` announces the failure, so it is what asks the question a reader asks next. At the two moments a budget is in trouble -- the 70% warning and the termination -- it prints sccache's own counters, and only when `RUSTC_WRAPPER` names sccache, so a budgeted step that compiles nothing stays exactly as quiet as before (`a_budget_that_expires_reports_the_compiler_cache_counters`, `a_budget_warning_reports_the_counters_without_touching_the_result`, `a_budget_that_wraps_no_compiler_reports_no_counters`; the first two fail against the previous script). This is the standing debug-output clause applied to CI: `Test (macos-15-intel / specification)` was terminated at its full 1200s budget still compiling dependencies, and the two candidate causes -- a slower runner, a colder compiler cache -- leave the same trace in the log, because cargo prints `Running \`sccache rustc ...\`` on a hit exactly as it does on a miss. Narrowing them took reconstructing per-crate rustc timestamps out of a megabyte of raw job log, and even that only ruled out a *partial* cache difference rather than closing the question, because the counters that would close it were never printed. The budget itself was not moved. See finding 34. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1021.rs`. |
| R1021-37 | A name is part of the interface, and a static analyser reads it as one. | Implemented: The `CodeQL` check reported 99 critical and high alerts on this branch, and every one of them was produced by an identifier's spelling. `rust/hard-coded-cryptographic-value` makes a sink of any argument reaching a parameter literally named `password`, `iv`, `nonce` or `salt`, so the `salt` parameter of `sample_index` -- an FNV-1a draw with no cryptography anywhere near it -- reported the 98 `temperature`, `guess_probability` and `questioning_rigor` literals that 24 files write into a `FormalizationSelectionConfig`; `rust/cleartext-logging` reads `session.?(id|key)` as account information, so `rust/src/cli_improve.rs` printing FNV-1a digests out of a binding called `session_id` reported as a leaked session token. The values are renamed after what they are (`seed`, `agent_session_digests`) with every seed string and every digest byte-identical before and after, and `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/codeql_sink_heuristics.rs` holds both heuristics over every Rust file CodeQL analyses rather than over the two sites that were caught -- the same file set, minus the prefixes `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` ignores, which `the_scan_skips_the_same_directories_the_codeql_config_ignores` keeps in step. What stays a finding rather than a change: the two `assert!` alerts in `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/issue_917.rs` and `_918.rs` are true positives over real Agent CLI session ids and are left open rather than spelled around or dismissed, and `salt`'s presence in the upstream sink list -- where `key` is already excluded as too false-positive prone -- is proposed as an upstream report rather than filed. See finding 36. |

## Issue #1073 Reasoning Standard: Unconditional Depth, Refutation First, Computed Trust

Issue [#1073](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1073) takes one
reference dialog -- a disk-space cleanup session -- and makes the properties that
made it good the *floor* rather than the ceiling. The instruction that governs
every row below is the one attached to that goal: the floor holds for the trivial
request too, and it is never conditional on being asked. See
`docs/case-studies/issue-1073/` for the case study and the contradiction audit.

The standard is data. `data/meta/reasoning-standard.lino` declares seven gates
(order, trigger, requirement, the reference behaviour it was adopted from, the
slug it reports on failure) and five numeric thresholds with the reason each
number is what it is; `rust/src/reasoning_standard/` loads it and evaluates every gate
as a pure predicate over a `ReasoningEpisode`. Nothing on that path consults a
model.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1073-1 | Deep reasoning everywhere: the reference depth is the floor, applies to trivial requests, and is never conditional on task difficulty or on prompting. | Delivered: Three defaults moved from the quiet setting to the full one: `RecursionMode::Down` -> `Both`, `SelectionMode::Off` -> `Record`, `SkillMode::Off` -> `Accumulate`, each reachable before only through `SolverConfig` or a `FORMAL_AI_*` variable. The reasoning-standard audit itself takes no mode at all: `record_meta_core` calls it unconditionally, and `the_meta_core_runs_the_audit_with_no_mode_in_front_of_it` fails if a condition is ever put in front of it. `open_episode` opens an episode from the formalization alone, so the greeting `hi` gets the same seven-gate ledger the reference dialog gets: `instruction_formalization` reports `Violated` with `courtesy:no_instructions_gathered` and `instruction_sources:0:required:2`, the other six report `NotTriggered` naming the trigger that was false, and the verdict is `not_confirmed_not_refuted` with its blockers named. The obligations are enumerated identically either way (`depth_floor_enumerates_every_gate_even_for_a_trivial_episode`, `the_depth_floor_holds_for_the_smallest_request_the_pipeline_can_formalize`, measured in `docs/case-studies/issue-1073/logs/reasoning-standard-audit.log`). |
| R1073-2 | Instructions for the task class are gathered and *formalized* into machine-checkable instruction sets, not paraphrased. Every attached required check must be observed before a step is complete. | Delivered: `rust/src/reasoning_standard/instructions.rs` compiles gathered steps into an ordered set; empty checks fail the gate, and `instruction_completion_requires_every_attached_check` rejects partial and duplicated observations. The set must draw on at least `minimum_instruction_sources` (2) distinct sources before a step counts as corroborated, since a single source cannot corroborate itself (`gathered_instructions_are_compiled_into_checkable_steps`). |
| R1073-3 | Official documentation and trustworthy sources are consulted as a default step of reasoning, not as an escalation. | Implemented: The `documentation_default` gate fires whenever any source was consulted and requires at least `minimum_documentation_sources` (1) of them to be primary for its subject -- the subject speaking about itself, or a first-hand record of it (`primary_documentation_is_required_by_default`). |
| R1073-4 | Source trust is computed from proximity to primary sources, never assumed; conflicts resolve toward the more primary source. | Delivered: `PrimacyChain::derive_trust` derives the tier from the chain's structure alone: an empty chain is `Unoriginal` for `NoPrimacyChain`, a hop that cannot name its upstream is `Unoriginal` for `UnfoundedStep`, distance zero is first-party or first-hand journalism, and a named upstream chain is independent corroboration. `resolve_conflict` prefers the shorter distance and answers `Unresolved` at equal distance rather than picking a side. The live registry is held to the same rule: every source in `data/seed/sources-registry.lino` declares a `primacy` chain citing the site's own policy, `SourceRecord::tier` is the derived value, `tier_from_seed` and its silent `_ => independent_corroboration` arm are deleted, and the hand-written tier survives only as `asserted_tier`, checked against the derivation (`source_trust_is_derived_from_the_primacy_chain`). |
| R1073-5 | Refutation first, with deliberate variety; only refuted refutations or a positively proven alternative permit leaning toward a conclusion, otherwise "not confirmed and not refuted" with the blockers named. | Implemented: The `refutation_variety` gate requires `minimum_refutation_attempts` (3) attempts with *distinct mechanisms* spanning `minimum_refutation_axis_kinds` (2) of the three kinds -- a different mechanism, a different source, a different denied assumption -- so three restatements of one doubt count as one. `Verdict::NotConfirmedNotRefuted` carries `blockers()`: the gates that failed and the checks that could not be run. It is the honest default, not a fallback (`conclusions_need_varied_refutations_before_they_may_be_leaned_toward`). |
| R1073-6 | Requirements 1-5 are formal checkable procedures, so the same conclusions stay reachable with the LLM removed. | Implemented: Every gate is a pure predicate over the episode record; `audit` reaches its verdict with no model in the loop, and `the_standard_is_a_formal_procedure_that_replays_without_a_model` replays the same episode to the same verdict and the same event payloads. The procedure is itself data: `data/meta/reasoning-standard-recipe.lino` declares the eight steps, the seven gates and the nine implementing functions, and `rust/tests/unit/specification/reasoning_standard_meta_algorithm.rs` fails when the recipe and the source disagree. |
| R1073-7 | Contradiction audit: enumerate what defines reasoning today, flag assumed trust, single-source conclusions and conditional depth, update each flagged place, and leave a regression derived from the reference dialog. | Implemented: `docs/case-studies/issue-1073/contradiction-audit.md` is the enumeration and the disposition of each finding, including the two places deliberately left unchanged and why. The regression is `data/meta/reasoning-standard-reference-episode.lino` -- the reference dialog with its project-specific tooling, absolute paths and session management dropped -- which clears all seven gates, together with the mutation set in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1073_reasoning_standard.rs` that makes each gate fail when the behaviour it enforces is removed. |

## Issue #1085 The Links Network Is Not The System That Reasons (E108)

Diagnosis issue [#1085](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1085);
case study in `docs/case-studies/issue-1085/`. Delivered items name the push
that landed them; the rest are in progress on the same pull request or are
sub-issues of #1085.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1085-1 | **Superseded, and the kernel/non-kernel split with it** (VISION.md, docs/architect-notes/). The requirement to name a Rust kernel and show the line count outside it falling at every release was never asked for; it entered through issue #918's acceptance criterion. Rust is one target the meta language is emitted into, so its line count measures an output and may grow while the algorithm becomes more general. | Superseded (see the requirement cell): the release-shrink rule is removed from `self-development-status.yml`. The shrink-only ceilings remain as an ordinary gate (`data/meta/debt-ratchet.lino`, `scripts/check-debt-ratchet.rs`, gate `check_debt_ratchet`): they move down and never up, and no release depends on them. |
| R1085-2 | Load seed and meta into the doublets store at startup and route matching through link queries; one generic interpreter for `when x do y` rules and `.lino` skills; migrate pending handlers smallest-first. | Delivered: `rust/src/seed_links.rs` projects every bundled seed document and the routing meta documents into one links network at startup and mirrors it into a native link-cli store beside the memory store when the server starts; handler precedence, cue lookup and intent routing read it through link queries (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1085_seed_links.rs` shows the former parsers and the queries agree); `rust/src/rule_interpreter.rs` walks `data/seed/handler-rules.lino`, eleven precedence names are data with their Rust deleted (ledger pending 51 to 40), and `rust/tests/unit/issue_1085_rule_interpreter.rs` routes an injected unseen intent in en, ru, hi, zh with no Rust change. Migration continues smallest-first. |
| R1085-3 | Express the ladder's three edit shapes as link substitutions over the meta-language CST network with reconstruct, rustfmt, `cargo check`, `cargo test`; resolve requirement-shaped edits by link query over the self-AST census. | Delivered: the three shapes run as link substitutions (`rust/src/agentic_coding/link_edit_rules.rs`); each of the 32 ladder leaves is a committed rule under `experiments/issue_1028_agent_cli_ladder/rules/` that `rust/tests/unit/issue_1085_requirement_resolution.rs` applies to the current source; a requirement that names behaviour and no file resolves through the self-AST census (`rust/src/agentic_coding/requirement_resolution.rs`), and every leaf requirement resolves to its leaf file. The bot-opened pull request is tracked under R1085-9. |
| R1085-4 | Attribute self-authored commits by the model that produced them: `Formal-AI-Model` must be formal-ai and be named in the committed evidence; a session or model naming a hosted model is not self-authored. | Delivered: `scripts/self-hosting-attribution.rs::model_attribution`; `rust/tests/unit/specification/self_hosting_metric.rs` fixtures carry the trailer. |

## Issue #1137 Pre-Merge Four-Client Routing Replay

Issue [#1137](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1137) records
that Agent, OpenCode, Claude, and Codex expose different tool vocabularies, so a
single-client or held-out-only pull-request gate cannot prove a routing change
before it reaches `main`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1137-1 | A pull request that changes agentic routing must run the full real-client replay before merge. | Implemented: `scripts/detect-code-changes.rs` derives `agentic-routing-changed` from the complete PR diff whenever a tracked path under `rust/src/agentic_coding/` changes; `.github/workflows/release.yml` passes `full-replay: true` to the reusable Agent CLI workflow for that PR. The path classifier and caller expression are pinned by `detect_code_changes::tests::agentic_source_changes_request_the_four_client_replay` and `ci_cd::issue_1137_agentic_routing_replay`. |
| R1137-2 | The pre-merge replay must retain Agent, OpenCode, Claude, and Codex and prove search, fetch, and cited synthesis. | Implemented: the full-replay-only `run_issue_781.sh` step retains the four-client default and its per-client search/fetch/final assertions; `the_full_replay_still_exercises_each_supported_client` pins the caller, harness, and client inventory. |
| R1137-3 | Pull requests outside the routing boundary should retain the cheaper held-out gate. | Implemented: the new detector output is false outside `rust/src/agentic_coding/`; the existing `main`, schedule, and manual full-replay conditions remain unchanged. The classifier regression exercises unrelated coding and documentation paths. |

## Issue #1138 Bottleneck Audit

This shard records the requirement contracts introduced while closing the
measured bottlenecks in issue #1138. A status below names the implementation and
the automated test that holds it; it does not claim a run that has not been
observed on the final tree.

| ID | Requirement | Status / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1138-B5-1 | Every satisfied obligation node must carry a matching execution record: the command, its exit code or an explicit none, and a SHA-256 of the exact observed bytes. | Implemented by `rust/src/execution_evidence.rs::Evidence::observed`, which hashes its raw byte slice, and by the evidence-bearing `ObligationOutcome::Satisfied` variant in `rust/src/obligation_ledger.rs`. Verified by `rust/tests/unit/specification/execution_evidence.rs` and `rust/tests/unit/specification/obligation_ledger.rs`. |
| R1138-B5-2 | An observation may discharge only the node whose expectation names its command or path; an unrelated result clears nothing. | Implemented by `rust/src/obligation_ledger.rs::ObligationLedger::observe`. Verified by `rust/tests/unit/specification/obligation_ledger.rs::an_unrelated_observation_discharges_nothing`. |
| R1138-B5-3 | A clause with no derivable expectation is split, not discarded; a clause that cannot be split is reported as an unsatisfied gap with its byte span, never as completion prose. | Implemented by `rust/src/obligation_ledger.rs::ObligationNode`, `rust/src/agentic_coding/task_obligations.rs` and the `ObligationStep::ReportGap` branch in `rust/src/agentic_coding/planner.rs`. Verified across ten prompts and five languages by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_obligation_evidence.rs`. |

## Issue #1138 Composition From Retrieved Sources

Retrieved procedure text — not an enumerated shape catalog — is the source of
coding answers. The steps are formalized into a language-neutral IR and lowered
per language; the seeded idiom catalog that bootstrapped this path is itself
deletable data whose loss is provably recoverable. The contract is covered by
`rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/` (procedure text, program IR, IR lowering,
composition search, multilingual parity) and the full-suite upstream rows in
`data/benchmarks/external-results.lino`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1138-B2-1 | Retrieved procedure text becomes an ordered, typed step list with per-step source spans, never a stored answer body. | Implemented by `coding_discovery::procedure_text`; covered by `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/procedure_text.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-2 | The ordered step list lowers into a language-neutral `ProgramIr` whose nodes carry types, fragments, grounding, and license metadata. | Implemented by `rust/src/coding/program_ir.rs`; covered by `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/program_ir.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-3 | The `ProgramIr` renders per target language — the lowerer is selected after composition and preserves the IR identity — and equivalent requirements in English, Russian, Hindi, Chinese, and Spanish expose the same frontier. | Implemented by IR lowering and Python rendering; covered by `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/ir_lowering.rs` and the 25 held-out cases in `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/multilingual.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-4 | The seeded idiom catalog is a deletable bootstrap: every fragment is declared `bootstrap true` with a rediscovery query, and deleting it loses no source evidence. | Implemented by `data/seed/coding-composition-fragments.lino`; covered by `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/fragment_catalog.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-5 | Forgetting a discovered procedure and rediscovering it from the same trusted sources reproduces the same content id. | Implemented by the discovered-procedure ledger; covered by `forgotten_procedures_are_rediscovered_from_the_same_sources` in `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/ledger.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-6 | The upstream coding suites are measured at full slice (HumanEval 164, MBPP 500), online and cold-offline, with per-slice floors and the recorded failure frontier — a first-20 score is a regression control, never a suite score. | Implemented: measured by `benchmark run --suite humaneval --slice 164` and `--suite mbpp --slice 500`, each cold-offline and with `--online`; rows recorded 2026-09-17 in `data/benchmarks/external-results.lino` with `--frontier-record`; floors enforced as best-measured pass counts by `external_benchmarks::ratchet`, verified by `rust/tests/unit/specification/external_benchmarks.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-7 | Every held-out structural answer reports a `typed_search(…)` composition over seed fragments, and no benchmark identifier, task sentence, assertion, or expected-output literal may leak into source or seed data — an example's expected value is payable only as a conditional branch payload, never as a condition operand. | Covered by `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/structural_composition.rs` and `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/no_memorization.rs`; the observation-literal slot filter is enforced in `rust/src/coding/composition_search.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-8 | OEIS and the Python standard-library documentation are selected through the trusted-source registry as declared sources with pinned extractors, endpoints, licenses, and content-addressed caches. | Implemented as declared trusted sources in `data/seed/sources-registry.lino` (`oeis`, `python_docs`); verified by the replay pins `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/oeis.rs` and `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/python_docs.rs`. |
